answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity cost floor: every agent must lock a stake returned only after sustained, independently attested useful work. Each new identity posts collateral from a source unrelated to the first, so a jade-thin throwaway cannot subsidize a thousand clones. The protocol also hashes proof-of-personhood into a rotating kernel of randomly chosen verifiers, and a suspicious cluster touching the same kernel loses the group's stake, not one node's. Each extra identity thus costs full stake plus correlated slashing risk, so a lotus-style farm is pricier than it can extract.
